**Test image key features:**
- Affected part: **stem** at an upper branch junction
- Brown necrotic lesion with **fine white/gray dusty sporulation** covering it
- Dead/wilted brown leaves nearby
- Green healthy tissue visible nearby

**Comparison summary:**
| Class | Match quality |
|-------|--------------|
| **Gray_Mold** | Best match — Botrytis produces fine dusty gray-white sporulation on necrotic stem lesions at junctions |
| Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot | White cottony mycelium + black sclerotia (not seen in test) |
| Southern_Blight | Soil-line disease, coarser mycelium |
| Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers | Some similarity but darker, underground cankers |
| All others | Leaf spots, fruit lesions, vascular wilt — not matching stem with sporulation |

The fine white/gray dusty powdery growth on the necrotic brown stem tissue at a branch junction is the hallmark of **Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold)**. The Gray Mold reference showed a matching stem lesion at a junction (image 1573933), and Botrytis is well-known for producing this exact grayish-white dusty sporulation pattern on necrotic stem tissue with associated dead leaves.
